verdict.rationale: Expensify documents its own credential issuance in two forms: server-to-server partnerUserID/partnerUserSecret pairs tied to a single account, and an OAuth2 authorization code flow that yields short-lived access tokens to act on behalf of individual users. This gives some per-user, time-limited bounding, but no permission scopes or least-privilege controls are documented. Missing for 10: documented permission scopes or granular per-credential permissions, read-only or limited-action credentials, agent-specific credential guidance, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: To act on behalf of individual Expensify users, use the OAuth2 authorization code flow to obtain a short-lived access token.
Credential based `partnerUserID` + `partnerUserSecret` Server-to-server integrations with a single Expensify account
A pair of credentials: `partnerUserID` and `partnerUserSecret` will be generated and shown on the page.
